description: Declared mutants of GYO::Base on the gyo2 line (ids bs-). The behaviour of IdIssuer and CurrentThreadSerial (engine/core/base/include/engine/base/IdIssuer.hpp), checked by gyo_base_tests (tests/common/base). Added by kernel-subtract-structure, S10 fix (docs/architecture/target/v2/kernel-subtract-structure-declaration.zh-Hant.md; user decision 2026-11-18, option (b)) and its adversarial check (Fable/high); kept in the kernel catalog until v8-arch-gyo2-move-bs-mutants (2026-11-19, follow-up of docs/architecture/target/v2/kernel-mutation-prune-report.zh-Hant.md) moved them here unchanged. bs-thread-serial-not-thread-local was merged into bs-thread-serial-issuer-per-thread before the move (kernel-mutation-subsumption-report.zh-Hant.md section 3). bs-id-issuer-not-atomic is probabilistic (8 threads x 10000). A mutant is killed only when its check fails with the expected message (AGENTS 14.2). Run from the repository root with python3 -I -B tests/common/mutation/run_mutations.py --catalog docs/architecture/target/v2/scripts/base_mutations.json --build-dir <build dir with tests> --cmake <cmake>.

mutants.what: IdIssuer::Next does not advance, so it hands one number out again (v8-arch-gyo2-kernel-subtract-structure, S10 fix: user decision 2026-11-18, option (b))
every IdIssuer shares one counter, so a second issuer continues the first one's numbers (v8-arch-gyo2-kernel-subtract-structure, S10 fix: user decision 2026-11-18, option (b))

IdIssuer::Next reads and writes the counter in two steps, so two threads can take one number (probabilistic: 8 threads x 10000) (v8-arch-gyo2-kernel-subtract-structure, S10 fix: user decision 2026-11-18, option (b))
mutants.replace:
const std::uint64_t id = next_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
        next_.store(id + 1, std::memory_order_relaxed);

mutants.what: CurrentThreadSerial takes a new number on every call instead of keeping the thread's first one (v8-arch-gyo2-kernel-subtract-structure, S10 fix: user decision 2026-11-18, option (b))
mutants.cases: CurrentThreadSerial: the same number on one thread*

mutants.what: the thread serials come from an issuer of each thread's own, so every thread gets 1 and a later thread repeats an earlier one's number (v8-arch-gyo2-kernel-subtract-structure, S10 fix: user decision 2026-11-18, option (b)) (v8-arch-gyo2-mutation-prune step 3, subsumption: merged in bs-thread-serial-not-thread-local [the serial is one variable for the process, not thread_local: every thread gets the first asker's number (adversarial check of the S10 fix, Fable/high; v8-arch-gyo2-kernel-subtract-structure)])
mutants.cases: CurrentThreadSerial: a thread started after another ended*

mutants.what: CurrentThreadSerial returns the address of the thread_local (the bug S10 fixes: macOS hands a ended thread's storage to a new thread) (adversarial check of the S10 fix, Fable/high; v8-arch-gyo2-kernel-subtract-structure)
mutants.cases: CurrentThreadSerial: a thread started after another ended*

mutants.what: IdIssuer starts at 0 and Next() does not assert: 0 is handed out (adversarial check of the S10 fix, Fable/high; v8-arch-gyo2-kernel-subtract-structure) (the assertion alone, for the 2^64-th number, is not reachable by a test: no mutant for it)
IdIssuer starts at 2 (adversarial check of the S10 fix, Fable/high; v8-arch-gyo2-kernel-subtract-structure)
the first thread to ask gets serial 0 (the issuer's number minus 1) (adversarial check of the S10 fix, Fable/high; v8-arch-gyo2-kernel-subtract-structure)
mutants.cases: CurrentThreadSerial: the same number on one thread*

mutants.what: a thread that is not the first to ask gets 0: only the main thread's serial is checked against 0 (adversarial check of the S10 fix, Fable/high; v8-arch-gyo2-kernel-subtract-structure)
mutants.replace:
if (Detail::threadSerial == 0) Detail::threadSerial = Detail::threadSerials.Next();
    return Detail::threadSerial == 5 ? 0 : Detail::threadSerial;
mutants.cases: CurrentThreadSerial: a thread started after another ended*
